item.title: Bain Exits Kioxia After Landmark Chip Deal Yields Record Returns
item.description: Bain Capital has sold its entire stake in flash memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings Corp., closing a chapter on a deal that’s transformed the Japanese tech and investment landscape.

item.title: Malaysia May Hold Policy Rate, Signal Upcoming Hike as AI Boosts Economic Growth
item.description: Malaysia will likely hold its benchmark interest rate on Thursday and signal a possible hike later this year as the artificial intelligence boom drives faster-than-expected economic growth.

item.title: Gold Holds Decline as US Strikes on Iran Magnify Inflation Risks
item.description: Gold held a decline as a second day of US strikes against Iran drove energy prices higher and intensified concerns around inflation.

item.title: Luxury Car Firm DuPont Registry Group to Pick Banks for IPO
item.description: DuPont Registry Group, a luxury car marketplace and media company, has picked banks for a US initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Nvidia Rival Positron Holds Talks to Raise Funds at $5 Billion Valuation
item.description: AI chip startup Positron is in talks to raise about $750 million in financing during a round with two phases, part of a groundswell of companies looking to compete with Nvidia Corp.

item.title: Samsung, SK Hynix and Leveraged ETFs Drive 70% of Korea Trading
item.description: Retail fervor over leveraged ETFs in South Korea has grown so intense that the products, together with the two chipmaker stocks they track, now make up more than 70% of trading value in the $4.3 trillion market.

item.title: Noteholders to Aston Martin Sign Cooperation Pact Amid Debt Rout
item.description: A group of creditors to luxury car maker Aston Martin has signed a cooperation pact as earnings pressure weighs on the company’s debt.

item.title: Harley-Davidson’s Credit Ratings Get Cut to Junk By S&P
item.description: S&P Global Ratings cut Harley-Davidson Inc.’s credit grades to junk status on Wednesday, citing the company’s strategy to start selling lower-cost motorcycles to boost revenue.

item.title: SK Hynix US Offering Is More Than Seven Times Oversubscribed
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s US listing is more than seven times oversubscribed, according to people familiar with the matter, as the South Korean memory chipmaker prepares to price its offering Thursday.

item.title: Oil Gains, US Stock Futures Drop on New Strikes: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil gained and US equity futures ticked lower after the US said it is striking Iran for the second straight day, an escalation of violence that threatens to choke shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Oil Extends Surge as Fresh US Strikes Against Iran Rattle Market
item.description: Oil extended a powerful surge as the US struck targets in Iran for a second day, raising risks for energy supplies from the region.

item.title: 【今朝の5本】仕事を始める前に読んでおきたい厳選ニュース
item.description: ​威嚇強める、FOMC議事要旨、テック起債、BofA姿勢転換、世界成長見通し

item.title: GrainCorp Pushes for Australia Biofuel Mandates After Iran War
item.description: Australia should adopt national biofuel mandates to bolster its energy security, according to GrainCorp Ltd., after months of uncertainty from the Iran war which sent shockwaves through the country’s economy.

item.title: Japan’s Rating Looks Stable Despite Spending Risks, Moody’s Says
item.description: The prospect of trillions of dollars of government spending that has rattled Japan’s bond and currency markets has yet to change views at Moody’s Ratings, at least for now.

item.title: US Judge Allows SEC-Musk Deal Despite ‘Significant Misgivings’
item.description: A US judge signed off on Elon Musk paying $1.5 million to end a Securities and Exchange Commission lawsuit that accused him of cheating Twitter Inc. investors when he missed a deadline in 2022 to disclose his growing stake in the company.

item.title: Hyperscaler Debt Is Now a Rates Story
item.description: When so much supply hits the market.

item.title: Accor to Tap Banks for Hoxton Owner Ennismore’s US IPO
item.description: Accor SA has lined up investment banks to arrange a potential US initial public offering of Ennismore Lifestyle Group Ltd., according to people familiar with the matter, as the French hotel group presses on with plans to spin out the unit.

item.title: Sonos Cuts Top Design and Product Executives as Part of Layoffs
item.description: Sonos Inc. has pushed out some of its top design and product management executives as part of job cuts in recent weeks, raising questions about the company’s ability to develop breakthrough products beyond its short-term hardware road map of safe bets.

item.title: Meta to Build First Data Center in Canada, Expanding Global Fleet
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. will invest around $10 billion to build its first data center in Canada as the company expands its infrastructure to support its artificial intelligence ambitions.

item.title: Top India Asset Manager Sets Price Range for $1.22 Billion IPO
item.description: SBI Funds Management Ltd.’s biggest investors are seeking to raise as much as 116.9 billion rupees ($1.22 billion) in what’s expected to be India’s first billion-dollar IPO of the year.

item.title: Los Angeles Hospital Blames Covid, Lender Dispute for Bankruptcy
item.description: Pacifica Hospital of the Valley, which serves poor and homeless residents in Los Angeles, filed for bankruptcy, blaming old financial problems linked to the Covid-19 pandemic and a more recent dispute with lenders.

item.title: US Consumer Borrowing Unexpectedly Drops by Most Since 2024
item.description: US consumer borrowing unexpectedly declined for the first time since 2024 on a drop in revolving credit.

item.title: Brazil Energy Firm Origem Is Said to Seek $2.5 Billion Valuation
item.description: Origem Energia SA, the Brazilian natural gas and oil company, is aiming for an enterprise value of $2 billion to $2.5 billion as it seeks strategic alternatives to raise capital, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Fed Minutes Show ‘a Few’ Officials Saw Case for June Hike
item.description: A few Federal Reserve officials in their most recent policy meeting said there was a case for raising interest rates, though they ultimately supported the decision to leave rates on hold.

item.title: Microsoft’s Xbox to Shift Obsidian Studio to New ‘Fallout’ Video Game
item.description: The game maker is also canceling a planned sequel to last year’s ‘Avowed’

item.title: Blackstone’s QTS Taps US Loan Market in Data Center-Backed Deal
item.description: QTS Realty Trust LLC is seeking to raise $2 billion to repay debt tied to US data centers and pay dividends to Blackstone Inc.

item.title: Record-High US Fuel Exports Are Straining Domestic Stockpiles
item.description: Unprecedented overseas demand for US diesel, propane and other fuels is straining commercial reserves from the Gulf Coast to the Eastern Seaboard as the US-Iran conflict reintensifies, pushing energy prices higher.

item.title: SpaceXAI, Cursor Unveil Grok AI Model for Legal, Finance Tasks
item.description: SpaceXAI has unveiled a new artificial intelligence model built in partnership with AI coding startup Cursor that’s meant to be more adept at finance, legal and coding tasks, in a bid by Elon Musk’s firm to gain ground on rivals like Anthropic PBC and OpenAI.

item.title: Shipowners Wrestle With Hormuz Risks as US-Iran Deal Crumbles
item.description: Shipowners painted a mixed picture of their willingness to continue transiting the Strait of Hormuz in the hours after President Donald Trump said the US ceasefire with Iran is “over.”

item.title: Parents’ Phone Addiction Affects Bond with Kids, New Study Finds
item.description: Parents’ attachment to screens and smartphones can have negative, long-lasting developmental and psychological effects on their children, according to new research.
